mainTopic: רבי שמעון's view of a פטר חמור after עריפה, and whether the רבנן hold הואיל ואיסורו חישובו for טומאת אוכלין
overview: Background: רבי שמעון holds that something which is אסור בהנאה cannot get טומאת אוכלין, because it does not count as 'food'. A ברייתא says he agrees that בשר בחלב can get טומאת אוכלין, 'because it once had a שעת הכושר.' The גמרא first asks why the ברייתא needs that reason, since רבי שמעון permits benefit from בשר בחלב (proven from another ברייתא). It answers that the ברייתא gives one reason and adds another (חדא ועוד). רבא then argues that if a פטר חמור were permitted after עריפה, the ברייתא would have listed it next to בשר בחלב. The גמרא pushes back: the ברייתא is speaking of a case where no one intended to eat the donkey. That raises the question of why the רבנן still treat it as food. The answer given is הואיל ואיסורו חישובו: its being forbidden counts as intent. The גמרא tests this principle against two משניות and deflects them by assigning them to רבי שמעון. A third source, from the רישא of the משנה in עוקצין, cannot be assigned to him. So רבא concludes that no one holds איסורו חישובו, and his new explanation continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Why does בשר בחלב need the שעת הכושר reason?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the reason the ברייתא gives for why בשר בחלב can get טומאת אוכלין according to רבי שמעון.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, why does the ברייתא say specifically that בשר בחלב can become impure because it once had a time when it was fit? Learn it instead from the fact that it is food you can give to others!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the reason the ברייתא gives for treating בשר בחלב as food. It points out that a simpler reason is available.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון's rule is that only food you are allowed to benefit from counts as 'food' for טומאה. If בשר בחלב is מותר בהנאה in his view, it is clearly 'food you can feed to others' (for example, you may give or sell it to a non-Jew). So why does the ברייתא use the more roundabout reason of שעת הכושר?

keyTerms.meaning: If so (if that is the case)
Why specifically this? Why single this out?
A time when it was fit (before the meat and milk were cooked together)
Derive it for me instead from…
Food that you are able to feed to others, which is רבי שמעון's definition of 'food'

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is not questioning whether בשר בחלב gets טומאה. Everyone here agrees that it does. The challenge is only about WHICH reason the ברייתא gives.

phrases.english: If so,
meat in milk, why specifically
phrases.notes: Why does the ברייתא give this particular reason?

phrases.english: because it had a period of fitness?
Derive it instead

phrases.aramaic: דְּאוֹכֶל שֶׁאַתָּה יָכוֹל לְהַאֲכִילוֹ לַאֲחֵרִים הוּא!
phrases.english: from the fact that it is food you can feed to others!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי הָכִי, בָּשָׂר בְּחָלָב מַאי אִירְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the wording of the ברייתא that רבא cited earlier on the daf.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's reason 'שהרי היתה לו שעת הכושר' for בשר בחלב.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: According to רבי שמעון, בשר בחלב is מותר בהנאה. It is therefore food you can feed to others, and the שעת הכושר reason seems unnecessary.

steps.title: Source that רבי שמעון permits benefit from בשר בחלב
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא backs up the premise of its challenge with a ברייתא: רבי שמעון holds בשר בחלב is forbidden to eat but permitted for benefit.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught: רבי שמעון בן יהודה says in the name of רבי שמעון: בשר בחלב is forbidden to eat but permitted for benefit. The verse says 'For you are a holy people to ה׳ your God,' and elsewhere it says 'And you shall be holy men to Me' (about טריפה). Just as there it is forbidden to eat but permitted for benefit, so too here it is forbidden to eat but permitted for benefit.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא proves the assumption behind its challenge, namely that רבי שמעון really does allow benefit from בשר בחלב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both verses use the word 'holy' (קדוש / קדש), and this links them to each other. The second verse is about טריפה, which may not be eaten but may be used for benefit (it can be thrown to dogs). So בשר בחלב gets the same rule: אסור באכילה, מותר בהנאה.

keyTerms.meaning: As it was taught in a ברייתא
Forbidden to eat
Permitted to benefit from
Elsewhere, in the other verse
Just as there… so too here (a comparison of two verses)

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the basis for רבי שמעון's well-known position that בשר בחלב is מותר בהנאה, which differs from the majority view.

phrases.english: As it was taught:

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן:
phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon ben Yehuda says in the name of Rabbi Shimon:
Meat in milk is forbidden to eat
and permitted for benefit,
as it says: 'For you are a holy people'
to ה׳ your God,'
phrases.notes: דברים 14:21, the verse about cooking a kid in its mother's milk

phrases.english: and elsewhere it says:
'And you shall be holy men to Me,'

phrases.aramaic: מָה לְהַלָּן אָסוּר בַּאֲכִילָה וּמוּתָּר בַּהֲנָאָה,
phrases.english: just as there it is forbidden to eat and permitted for benefit,

phrases.aramaic: אַף כָּאן אָסוּר בַּאֲכִילָה וּמוּתָּר בַּהֲנָאָה!
phrases.english: so too here it is forbidden to eat and permitted for benefit!

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא, רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the source for the premise of the challenge in step 1.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי שמעון holds בשר בחלב is מותר בהנאה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא comparing the word 'holy' in the verses of בשר בחלב and טריפה.

steps.title: The ברייתא gives one reason and adds another
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the ברייתא gives two reasons: the food can be given to others, and in addition, even for a Jew it was once fit.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is saying one reason and then another. One: it is food you can feed to others. And another: even for the Jew himself, it once had a time when it was fit.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. It explains that the ברייתא does not reject the simple reason; it adds a second one on top of it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first reason, that it can be fed to others, is the obvious one and goes without saying. The ברייתא adds a stronger point: even for the Jew who may not eat it now, the meat and milk were each fit to eat before they were cooked together. Because the ברייתא writes out only the second reason, that does not mean the first reason is absent.

keyTerms.meaning: It states one reason and adds another
Even for him (the Jew himself)
Behold, after all

phrases.english: It states one reason and another:

phrases.aramaic: חֲדָא — דְּאוֹכֶל שֶׁאַתָּה יָכוֹל לְהַאֲכִילוֹ לַאֲחֵרִים הוּא,
phrases.english: One: it is food that you can feed to others,
and another: even for him himself
it had a time when it was fit.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the challenge raised in step 1.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpretation of the wording: the ברייתא gives an additional reason and does not replace the obvious one.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא's use of שעת הכושר implied that it did not accept the 'feed to others' reason.
steps.terutzMaskana: Both reasons apply. The ברייתא states the second, stronger one, and the first is taken for granted.

steps.title: Finishing רבא's proof about the פטר חמור
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to רבא's proof. If רבי שמעון permitted a פטר חמור after עריפה, the ברייתא should have listed it next to בשר בחלב as an exception.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if it were true that רבי שמעון permits a פטר חמור after its neck is broken, the ברייתא should have taught: 'And רבי שמעון agrees about a פטר חמור and בשר בחלב, that they can get טומאת אוכלין!'
steps.whatsHappening: Now that the side question about בשר בחלב is settled, the גמרא completes רבא's proof that רבי שמעון holds a פטר חמור is אסור בהנאה even after עריפה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא lists only בשר בחלב as an exception to רבי שמעון's rule that forbidden-for-benefit items are not 'food.' If a פטר חמור became permitted after עריפה, it would also be food you can feed to others, so it should appear in that list too. Since it is missing, רבי שמעון must hold that it stays אסור בהנאה.

keyTerms.meaning: And if it were so
Breaking the neck (of the פטר חמור)
A firstborn donkey
Let it teach; the ברייתא should have said
The impurity that applies to food

steps.whatToRemember: רבא's proof: the ברייתא lists only בשר בחלב, and not a פטר חמור, as forbidden food that still gets טומאת אוכלין. So רבי שמעון seems to hold that a פטר חמור stays אסור בהנאה after עריפה. Step 5 challenges this inference.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is רבא's proof about רבי שמעון's view of a פטר חמור after עריפה. The very next step pushes back on it by limiting the ברייתא to a case without intent.

phrases.english: And if it were so
that after breaking the neck Rabbi Shimon permits it,
let it teach: And Rabbi Shimon agrees
regarding a firstborn donkey and meat in milk
that they become impure with food impurity!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִם אִיתָא דִּלְאַחַר עֲרִיפָה שָׁרֵי רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the side challenge is resolved, returns to complete רבא's main proof.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי שמעון holds a פטר חמור is אסור בהנאה after עריפה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The silence of the ברייתא, which lists only בשר בחלב as an exception.

steps.title: The case is one where nobody intended to eat the donkey
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects רבא's proof. If someone intended the donkey for eating, רבי שמעון would agree it is food. The ברייתא is dealing with a case where no one intended it as food.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he intended it for eating, then yes, it would be food. Here we are dealing with a case where he did not intend it for eating.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the proof from Step 4. It explains why the ברייתא did not list פטר חמור next to בשר בחלב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא argued that רבי שמעון must forbid benefit from a פטר חמור, or else the ברייתא would have listed it as an exception. The גמרא answers that the ברייתא is talking about a case with no intent to eat. Donkey meat is not normal food, even for non-Jews. So without a plan to eat it, it is not food anyway, whether benefit is allowed or not.

keyTerms.meaning: He intended it (to be used as food)
So too; yes, that is indeed true
Here, with what case are we dealing? (narrows the case)

steps.confusionAlert: This does not mean רבי שמעון holds that a פטר חמור can never be food. It only means that in the specific case of the ברייתא, there was no intent, so it does not count as food.

phrases.english: If he intended it [to be eaten],
so too [it would be susceptible as food];
phrases.notes: Benefit is permitted, so it could be given to a non-Jew to eat.

phrases.english: here, with what are we dealing?
Where he did not intend it [to be eaten].
phrases.notes: Donkey meat is not ordinarily eaten, so without intent it is not food.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof brought in Step 4 by limiting the ברייתא to a case without intent.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: רבא's inference that the ברייתא's silence proves רבי שמעון forbids benefit from a פטר חמור.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The ברייתא is dealing with a case where no one intended to eat the donkey. Its silence therefore says nothing about whether benefit is allowed.

steps.title: Why do the רבנן still consider it food?
steps.stepSummary: If nobody intended to eat the donkey, why do the רבנן say it can become impure as food?
steps.simpleTranslation: And what is the reason the רבנן make it susceptible to impurity?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a follow-up question about the other side of the מחלוקת. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 5 said the case involves no intent to eat. Normally, something not usually eaten needs intent before it counts as food. So the גמרא wants to know how the רבנן can call it food without any intent.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the reason?
They rule it can become impure
The Sages (the majority opinion)

phrases.english: And what is the reason the Rabbis deem it susceptible to impurity?
phrases.notes: That is, even though no one intended to eat it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on Step 5's claim that the case involves no intent and asks how the רבנן's ruling fits that case.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reasoning behind the רבנן's view that a פטר חמור without intent can still receive טומאת אוכלין.

steps.title: Its prohibition counts as its intent
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן told רב ששת that the reason of the רבנן in the dispute is הואיל ואיסורו חישובו: the very fact that it is forbidden gives it the importance of food.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן said before רב ששת: because its prohibition is its intent.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from Step 6 by quoting a teaching said in front of רב ששת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Usually you need a person's plan (מחשבה) to make an unusual item count as food. The רבנן hold that when the Torah forbids eating something, that prohibition itself shows it is food-like. The prohibition replaces the person's intent.

keyTerms.meaning: Since its prohibition is its 'intent': being forbidden makes it count as food
The Sages said it in front of (a teacher)
An אמורא in whose presence this was said

steps.whyThisMatters: The principle הואיל ואיסורו חישובו is the center of the rest of this passage. The next challenge attacks whether the רבנן really hold it.

phrases.english: The Sages said it before Rav Sheshet:
Since its prohibition is its intent.
phrases.notes: The fact that eating it is forbidden makes it significant like food.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly answers the question of Step 6.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The רבנן hold הואיל ואיסורו חישובו: the prohibition itself acts as intent, so no human intent is needed.

steps.title: A משנה about a נבלת עוף טהור seems to contradict this principle
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the claim that the רבנן hold הואיל ואיסורו חישובו. A משנה says a נבלת עוף טהור needs intent before it can become impure as food. Yet a נבלה is forbidden to eat, so by this principle it should not need intent.
steps.simpleTranslation: But do the רבנן really say 'since its prohibition is its intent'? We learned: thirteen things were said about the carcass of a kosher bird, and this is one of them: it needs intent, but it does not need הכשר. If its prohibition is its intent, why do I need intent?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer of Step 7 by quoting a משנה from טהרות that seems to go against it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A נבלת עוף טהור is forbidden to eat, just like the פטר חמור. If being forbidden counts as intent, then the bird should not need any separate מחשבה. But the משנה, which seems to follow the majority view, says it does need מחשבה. That suggests the רבנן do not hold this principle.

keyTerms.meaning: But didn't we learn in a משנה?
The carcass of a kosher bird that was not properly slaughtered
Intent (here: a plan to use it as food)
Being made wet by a liquid, which normally readies food to become impure

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up מחשבה and הכשר. The משנה says this bird needs מחשבה (intent to eat it) but does NOT need הכשר (contact with liquid). The challenge is only about the מחשבה part.

phrases.english: But according to the Rabbis, do they say
'since its prohibition is its intent'?
But didn't we learn [in a mishna]:
They stated thirteen matters
concerning the carcass of a kosher bird,
and this is one of them:
it requires intent,
phrases.notes: Intent that it will be eaten, since most people do not eat it.

phrases.english: but it does not require being rendered susceptible [by liquid].
And if its prohibition is its intent,
why do I need intent?
phrases.notes: A נבלה is forbidden to eat, so its prohibition should already count as intent.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּלְרַבָּנַן מִי אָמַר הוֹאִיל וְאִיסּוּרוֹ חִישּׁוּבוֹ? וְהָא תְּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer given in Step 7 using a contradicting משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the רבנן hold הואיל ואיסורו חישובו.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A נבלת עוף טהור is forbidden to eat, yet the משנה requires separate מחשבה for it. If the prohibition counted as intent, that requirement would be unnecessary.

steps.title: That משנה follows רבי שמעון
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the משנה about the bird follows רבי שמעון. He does not hold הואיל ואיסורו חישובו, so it says nothing against the רבנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whose view is this? It is רבי שמעון.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא resolves the challenge of Step 8 by assigning the משנה to רבי שמעון rather than the רבנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The contradiction exists only if the משנה reflects the רבנן's view. By saying the משנה follows רבי שמעון, the גמרא removes the problem. רבי שמעון requires real intent, and the רבנן can still hold that a prohibition serves as intent.

keyTerms.meaning: Whose view is this?
It is (the view of) רבי שמעון

steps.whatToRemember: At this point the גמרא defends the claim that the רבנן hold הואיל ואיסורו חישובו by assigning the משנה to רבי שמעון. This defense does not hold up: steps 11–13 refute it, and רבא drops the principle in step 14.

phrases.english: In accordance with whom is this?
It is Rabbi Shimon.
phrases.notes: He does not hold that a prohibition serves as intent.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the contradiction raised in Step 8.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Attributing the source to a different תנא (מאן תנא)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה about the bird reflects the רבנן's view, which would show they do not hold הואיל ואיסורו חישובו.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה follows רבי שמעון, who rejects the principle. The רבנן can still hold it.

steps.title: A second משנה (עוקצין) challenges the principle, with the same answer
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a second משנה (עוקצין): a non-kosher animal carcass anywhere, and a kosher bird carcass or fat in the villages, all need intent before they can become impure as food. If being forbidden counts as intent, why is intent needed? The answer is the same as before: this משנה follows רבי שמעון.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: A carcass of a non-kosher animal in any place, and a carcass of a kosher bird, and fat in the villages, need intent, but do not need הכשר. If you say its prohibition gives it importance, why do I need intent? Whose view is this? It is רבי שמעון.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second challenge to הואיל ואיסורו חישובו from a different משנה, in עוקצין. It answers it the same way as in step 9, by assigning the משנה to רבי שמעון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: All the items listed are forbidden to a Jew. If איסורו חישובו were true, they should count as food without any intent. The גמרא again turns this aside by saying the משנה follows רבי שמעון. That leaves the רבנן free to hold the principle, which sets up the stronger challenge in steps 11–13.

keyTerms.meaning: Come and hear. This opens a proof from a source.
The carcass of a non-kosher animal
In the villages, where people do not usually eat these items.

steps.confusionAlert: This is a new source, not a repeat of steps 8–9. Step 8 quoted the משנה in טהרות about the kosher bird. This step quotes a different משנה, in עוקצין, which also covers non-kosher animals and fat. The answer is the same (it follows רבי שמעון).

phrases.english: Come and hear:
A carcass of a non-kosher animal, in any place,
and a carcass of a kosher bird
and forbidden fat, in the villages
need intent,
but do not need to be made susceptible by liquid.
And if you say its prohibition counts as its intent,
phrases.notes: This is the principle being tested.

phrases.english: why do I need intent?
Whose view is this? It is רבי שמעון.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע: נִבְלַת בְּהֵמָה טְמֵאָה בְּכׇל מָקוֹם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second challenge to the same claim from a different משנה (עוקצין), answered the same way as in step 9.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the רבנן hold הואיל ואיסורו חישובו.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Forbidden items still need intent, so being forbidden does not supply the intent.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Assigning the source to a different תנא (רבי שמעון).

steps.title: A second proof from the next part of the same משנה
steps.stepSummary: The משנה continues: a kosher animal carcass, a kosher bird carcass, and fat found in the markets need neither intent nor הכשר. The גמרא infers that a non-kosher animal does need intent, which goes against איסורו חישובו.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: A carcass of a kosher animal in any place, and a carcass of a kosher bird, and fat in the markets, need neither intent nor הכשר. This implies that a non-kosher animal does need intent.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another line from the same משנה. It reads it carefully to show that a non-kosher animal needs intent.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says only the kosher animal is exempt from needing intent. So a non-kosher animal, which is forbidden, still needs intent. That is the opposite of what איסורו חישובו would predict.

keyTerms.meaning: A kosher species of animal.
In the markets of big cities, where some people do eat these items.
This implies that a non-kosher one does need it. This is an inference from what the משנה chose to say.

phrases.english: Come and hear:
A carcass of a kosher animal, in any place,
and a carcass of a kosher bird
and forbidden fat, in the markets
need neither intent nor being made susceptible by liquid.
This implies that a non-kosher animal does need intent.
phrases.notes: The inference that drives the challenge.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע: נִבְלַת בְּהֵמָה טְהוֹרָה בְּכׇל מָקוֹם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new challenge to the same claim, from the next line of the same משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The רבנן holding הואיל ואיסורו חישובו.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: By inference, a forbidden non-kosher animal needs intent, so being forbidden does not count as intent.

steps.title: Blocking the escape that this is also רבי שמעון
steps.stepSummary: You cannot say this part of the משנה follows רבי שמעון. The סיפא is openly רבי שמעון, so the unnamed רישא must be the רבנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you will say: whose view is this? It is רבי שמעון. But since the end section is רבי שמעון, the beginning section is not רבי שמעון.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sees the answer someone might give, which is the same answer as in step 10, and shuts it down ahead of time.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When a משנה names רבי שמעון only in its סיפא, that signals that the unnamed רישא is the other view, the רבנן. So the inference from step 11 is a statement of the רבנן, and the challenge stands.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you will say. The גמרא brings up an answer in order to reject it.
The first section of a source.
The last section of a source.

phrases.english: And if you will say:
Whose view is this? It is רבי שמעון.
But since the end section is רבי שמעון,
the beginning section is not רבי שמעון.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי תֵּימָא: הָא מַנִּי רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Blocks the step 10 style of answer from being used on the step 11 challenge.
steps.kashyaTarget: The possible answer that the רישא follows רבי שמעון.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A named סיפא means the unnamed רישא is the other side, the רבנן.

steps.title: Quoting the סיפא to prove it is רבי שמעון
steps.stepSummary: The סיפא says רבי שמעון holds that even the camel, hare, hyrax and pig need neither intent nor הכשר, because they have some kosher signs. So the סיפא is clearly רבי שמעון, and the רישא is the רבנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: As the end section teaches: רבי שמעון says, even the camel, the hare, the hyrax and the pig need neither intent nor הכשר. And רבי שמעון said: what is the reason? Since they have signs of being kosher.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the סיפא to prove it is רבי שמעון's view. That locks in that the רישא belongs to the רבנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון makes these four animals easier because each has one kosher sign, which makes them closer to normal food. He does not say it is because they are forbidden. So the רבנן in the רישא require intent for non-kosher animals, and איסורו חישובו cannot be their view.

keyTerms.meaning: As it teaches. Used when quoting a source.
Camel, hare, hyrax, pig. Each has only one of the two kosher signs.
Signs of a kosher animal, such as split hooves or chewing the cud.

steps.whyThisMatters: This proves the רבנן require intent for a forbidden animal. That ends the הואיל ואיסורו חישובו explanation from step 7.

phrases.english: As the end section teaches:
רבי שמעון says:
even the camel and the hare
and the hyrax and the pig

phrases.aramaic: אֵינָן צְרִיכִין לֹא מַחְשָׁבָה וְלֹא הֶכְשֵׁר.
phrases.english: need neither intent nor being made susceptible by liquid.
And רבי שמעון said: what is the reason?
Since they have signs of being kosher.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the textual proof for the claim in step 12.
steps.raayaObject: That the סיפא is רבי שמעון, so the רישא is the רבנן, who require intent for a non-kosher animal.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The סיפא of the משנה in עוקצין, quoting רבי שמעון by name with his reasoning.

steps.title: רבא: nobody holds that being forbidden makes something food
steps.stepSummary: Since איסורו חישובו failed, רבא starts over. Everyone agrees we do not say it. If one broke the donkey's neck, the רבנן also agree it does not become impure as food. The sentence continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבא said: everyone agrees we do not say its prohibition counts as its intent. And if its neck was broken, so too it does not become impure as food.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives up the הואיל ואיסורו חישובו explanation entirely. רבא begins a new way to explain the רבנן in the firstborn donkey case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא says neither side holds איסורו חישובו. So in the plain case where the donkey's neck was broken and no one intended to eat it, even the רבנן agree it cannot become impure as food. רבא's sentence continues on the next amud, where he will explain what the רבנן and רבי שמעון actually disagree about.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather. This signals the earlier approach is being dropped.
Everyone agrees.
Its neck was broken. This is the required עריפה of a פטר חמור that was not redeemed.
So too. The ruling is the same here.

steps.whatToRemember: The idea that being forbidden gives something food importance is rejected by everyone. The donkey dispute must be explained some other way.

phrases.english: Rather, Rava said:
according to everyone, we do not say
that its prohibition counts as its intent,
and if its neck was broken,
so too it does not become impure as food,
phrases.notes: רבא's statement continues on the next amud.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר רָבָא: דְּכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא לָא אָמְרִינַן אִיסּוּרוֹ חִישּׁוּבוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Accepts the force of steps 11 to 13 and replaces the step 7 explanation.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Retracting the principle and building a new explanation of the dispute.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The רבנן treat the donkey as food because being forbidden gives it importance.
steps.terutzMaskana: No one holds איסורו חישובו. In the plain neck-breaking case, the רבנן agree it is not food. The real dispute is explained in what follows.
